title: Workers' compensation: Michigan law, the policy and premium
summary: Michigan's comp act, the federal acts, the six-part WC policy, and how to figure premium from payroll, rate and experience mod.
objectives: Explain the exclusive remedy and which Michigan employers must carry comp
Tell covered from uncovered injuries; know the waiting period and 80% benefit
Match the federal acts to the right workers and name the policy's six parts
Compute WC premium from payroll, rate and experience mod

scenes.title: Workers' compensation
scenes.subtitle: Michigan's act, the federal acts, the six-part policy, and the premium math

beats.text: Workers' comp is 5% of your exam, about 8 questions.
beats.say: Workers' comp is five percent of your exam, about eight questions.

beats.text: In this lesson: who must carry it, what it pays, federal acts, the policy, and premium math.
beats.say: In this lesson: who must carry it, what it pays, federal acts, the policy, and premium math.

items.label: Comp is the only remedy
items.detail: Against the employer, for a work injury or occupational disease

items.label: One exception: an intentional tort
items.detail: A deliberate act; the employer specifically intended an injury

items.label: Deemed intent
items.detail: Actual knowledge an injury was certain, willfully disregarded

items.label: Not enough: negligence
items.detail: Even gross negligence is not an intentional tort

beats.text: In Michigan, comp benefits are the employee's exclusive remedy against the employer.
beats.say: In Michigan, comp benefits are the employee's exclusive remedy against the employer.

beats.text: The only exception is an intentional tort: a deliberate act with specific intent to injure.
beats.say: The only exception is an intentional tort: a deliberate act with specific intent to injure.

beats.text: Intent is deemed if the employer knew an injury was certain and willfully disregarded it.
beats.say: Intent is deemed if the employer knew an injury was certain and willfully disregarded it.

beats.text: Here's the trap: even gross negligence isn't enough, and knowing an injury was possible isn't knowing it was certain.
beats.say: Here's the trap: even gross negligence isn't enough, and knowing an injury was possible isn't knowing it was certain.

scenes.title: Michigan: which employers must carry comp
scenes.hook: 3 at once, or 1 at 35 for 13 (out of the last 52). Public employers: every one, any size.
items: 3 at once: private non-farm employers regularly employing 3 or more at one time
1 at 35 for 13: fewer than 3, but 1 works 35+ hours a week for 13+ of the last 52 weeks
Public employers: all of them, regardless of the number of employees
Farms and household workers have their own special rules

beats.text: Who must carry comp in Michigan? The hook: 3 at once, or 1 at 35 for 13, out of the last 52. Public employers: every one, any size.
beats.say: Who must carry comp in Michigan? The hook: three at once, or one at thirty-five for thirteen, out of the last fifty-two. Public employers: every one, any size.

beats.text: A private, non-farm employer with fewer than 3 is covered if 1 works 35 hours or more a week for 13 weeks or more of the last 52.
beats.say: A private, non-farm employer with fewer than three is covered if one works thirty-five hours or more a week for thirteen weeks or more of the last fifty-two.

beats.text: Farms and household workers have special rules. Watch out: payroll size doesn't decide it.
beats.say: Farms and household workers have special rules. Watch out: payroll size doesn't decide it.

scenes.title: Michigan: what counts as a work injury

columns.name: Covered
points: Arises out of and in the course of employment
On the premises a reasonable time before or after work
Disease characteristic of and peculiar to the business

columns.name: Not covered
points: Activity whose major purpose is social or recreational
Ordinary disease of life the public is exposed to
Injury from the employee's intentional, willful misconduct

scenes.tell: The test is the work connection: arising out of and in the course of employment, not fault.

beats.text: Under Michigan's act, comp covers an injury arising out of and in the course of employment, with no need to prove the employer was negligent.
beats.say: Under Michigan's act, comp covers an injury arising out of and in the course of employment, with no need to prove the employer was negligent.

beats.text: On the premises a reasonable time before or after work, a worker is presumed to be in the course of employment. A disease characteristic of and peculiar to the business counts too.
beats.say: On the premises a reasonable time before or after work, a worker is presumed to be in the course of employment. A disease characteristic of and peculiar to the business counts too.

beats.text: Not covered: an activity whose major purpose is social or recreational, an ordinary disease of life, or the employee's intentional and willful misconduct.
beats.say: Not covered: an activity whose major purpose is social or recreational, an ordinary disease of life, or the employee's intentional and willful misconduct.

scenes.q: Maria twists her knee at her employer's bowling night, an event whose major purpose is social. Under Michigan's act, her injury is:
choices: Covered, because the employer sponsored the event
Covered only if it happened on the employer's premises
scenes.why: An injury from an activity whose major purpose is social or recreational is not covered by the act, even on the employer's premises.

beats.text: Maria hurts her knee at her employer's bowling night, whose major purpose is social. Is she covered? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Maria hurts her knee at her employer's bowling night, whose major purpose is social. Is she covered? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Not covered by the act. An activity whose major purpose is social or recreational is excluded, even on the employer's premises.
reveal.say: Not covered by the act. An activity whose major purpose is social or recreational is excluded, even on the employer's premises.

scenes.title: Michigan: waiting period and weekly benefit
scenes.hook: Wait 7, paid from day 8, back-paid at 2 weeks. Then 80% of after-tax wages, capped at 90% of the state average.
items: Wait 7: nothing is paid unless the incapacity lasts at least 1 week
Day 8: pay starts; at 2 weeks or longer, it's computed from the date of injury
80% of the after-tax average weekly wage for total disability
Cap: 90% of the state average weekly wage, set each January 1

beats.text: Now Michigan's benefits. The hook: wait 7, paid from day 8, back-paid at 2 weeks. Then 80% of after-tax wages, capped at 90% of the state average.
beats.say: Now Michigan's benefits. The hook: wait seven, paid from day eight, back-paid at two weeks. Then eighty percent of after-tax wages, capped at ninety percent of the state average.

beats.text: Nothing is paid unless incapacity lasts at least a week. Pay starts on day 8; at 2 weeks or longer, it's computed from the date of injury.
beats.say: Nothing is paid unless incapacity lasts at least a week. Pay starts on day eight; at two weeks or longer, it's computed from the date of injury.

beats.text: Watch out: 90% is the cap, not the benefit.
beats.say: Watch out: ninety percent is the cap, not the benefit.

scenes.title: Federal acts: rails, shore, ship
scenes.src: 45 USC 51, 53; 33 USC 902(3), 903(a), 904(b); 46 USC 30104(a); NCCI WC 00 00 00 C, Gen. C and Part Two C

columns.name: FELA
points: Sue for damages; must show railroad negligence
Own negligence reduces recovery, doesn't bar it

columns.name: Longshore Act (USL&HW)
points: Longshore and harbor workers, ship repairers
Navigable waters, piers, wharves, dry docks

columns.name: Jones Act
points: Seamen: a vessel's master and crew
Sue the employer, with a jury trial

scenes.tell: Railroad worker: FELA. Dock or shipyard worker: Longshore Act. Ship's crew: Jones Act.

beats.text: Three federal laws sit outside Michigan's act. First, FELA: interstate railroad workers sue for damages, proving the railroad's negligence. Their own negligence only reduces recovery.
beats.say: Three federal laws sit outside Michigan's act. First, F E L A: interstate railroad workers sue for damages, proving the railroad's negligence. Their own negligence only reduces recovery.

beats.text: Second, the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act pays no-fault benefits to maritime workers, like ship repairers, on navigable waters, piers and dry docks.
beats.say: Second, the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act pays no-fault benefits to maritime workers, like ship repairers, on navigable waters, piers and dry docks.

beats.text: Third, the Jones Act: a ship's crew member sues the employer with a jury trial. Rails, shore, ship. On a standard comp policy, all three need endorsements.
beats.say: Third, the Jones Act: a ship's crew member sues the employer with a jury trial. Rails, shore, ship. On a standard comp policy, all three need endorsements.

scenes.q: A cook who is a crew member on a Great Lakes freighter is hurt aboard and sues his employer before a jury. Which law is he using?
choices: The Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act
scenes.why: The Jones Act lets an injured seaman (a vessel's crew member) sue the employer with a jury trial. The Longshore Act excludes crew; FELA is for railroad workers.

beats.text: A cook on a Great Lakes freighter, a crew member, is hurt aboard and sues his employer before a jury. Which law? Pick an answer.
beats.say: A cook on a Great Lakes freighter, a crew member, is hurt aboard and sues his employer before a jury. Which law? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The Jones Act, the law for a ship's crew. The Longshore Act excludes crew, and FELA is for railroads.
reveal.say: The Jones Act, the law for a ship's crew. The Longshore Act excludes crew, and F E L A is for railroads.

scenes.title: The WC policy's six parts
scenes.src: NCCI WC 00 00 00 C (Ed. 1-15), Parts One to Six; MCL 418.621(4)(g); Michigan Law Endorsement WC 21 03 04
scenes.hook: Six C's, in order: 1 Comp, 2 Court (employers liability suits), 3 Crossing state lines, 4 Call us at once, 5 Cash (premium), 6 Conditions.
items: 1 Comp: benefits the law requires, no dollar limit. 2 Court: employers liability, with limits
3 Crossing state lines: states listed in Item 3.C. 4 Call us at once after an injury
5 Cash: the premium shown is an estimate; an audit sets the final premium
6 Conditions: insurer gives 10 days' cancel notice; in Michigan, a 20-day agency filing too

beats.text: The policy has six parts. Remember six C's: comp, court, crossing state lines, call us at once, cash, and conditions.
beats.say: The policy has six parts. Remember six C's: comp, court, crossing state lines, call us at once, cash, and conditions.

beats.text: Part One pays the benefits the comp law requires, with no dollar limit. Part Two, employers liability, has limits. Part Three applies to states listed in Item 3.C.
beats.say: Part One pays the benefits the comp law requires, with no dollar limit. Part Two, employers liability, has limits. Part Three applies to states listed in Item three C.

beats.text: Part Four: tell the insurer at once. Part Five: the premium is an estimate until the audit. Part Six: the insurer cancels on at least 10 days' notice; in Michigan it also files with the state agency at least 20 days ahead.
beats.say: Part Four: tell the insurer at once. Part Five: the premium is an estimate until the audit. Part Six: the insurer cancels on at least ten days' notice; in Michigan it also files with the state agency at least twenty days ahead.

scenes.title: Figuring the premium
scenes.src: NCRB Basic Manual Rule 5; IRMI 'manual premium', 'standard premium', 'premium discount'; NCCI WC 00 00 00 C, Part Five

beats.text: Rates are per $100 of payroll. Payroll is $250,000, the rate is $4, and the mod is 0.85.
beats.say: Rates are per one hundred dollars of payroll. Payroll is two hundred fifty thousand dollars, the rate is four dollars, and the mod is zero point eight five.

beats.text: Payroll divided by 100 is 2,500. Times $4, the manual premium is $10,000.
beats.say: Payroll divided by one hundred is two thousand five hundred. Times four dollars, the manual premium is ten thousand dollars.

beats.text: A mod under 1 is a credit; over 1 is a debit. $10,000 times 0.85 is $8,500, the standard premium.
beats.say: A mod under one is a credit; over one is a debit. Ten thousand dollars times zero point eight five is eight thousand five hundred dollars, the standard premium.

beats.text: A premium discount for larger policies comes after the mod.
beats.say: A premium discount for larger policies comes after the mod.

scenes.q: Payroll is $100,000, the rate is $5.00 per $100 of payroll, and the experience mod is 1.25. What is the premium after the mod?
scenes.why: $100,000 divided by 100 is 1,000. Times $5.00 is $5,000 manual premium. A 1.25 mod is a debit: $5,000 times 1.25 is $6,250.

beats.text: Your turn. Payroll is $100,000, the rate is $5, and the mod is 1.25. What's the premium after the mod? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Your turn. Payroll is one hundred thousand dollars, the rate is five dollars, and the mod is one point two five. What's the premium after the mod? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: $6,250. Payroll divided by 100 is 1,000, times $5 is $5,000, times the 1.25 debit mod.
reveal.say: Six thousand two hundred fifty dollars. Payroll divided by one hundred is one thousand, times five dollars is five thousand dollars, times the one point two five debit mod.

reveal.text: $5,000 forgets the mod; $3,750 treats the debit as a credit.
reveal.say: Five thousand dollars forgets the mod; three thousand seven hundred fifty dollars treats the debit as a credit.

scenes.title: Other ways to secure comp
scenes.src: MCL 418.611(1)-(2); MCL 418.201 and compiler's notes; MCL 500.2301; NCCI WC 00 03 11 A

items.label: Self-insure
items.detail: Authorized by the Workers' Disability Compensation Agency (not DIFS), on proof of solvency

items.label: Group self-insurance
items.detail: 2 or more employers in the same industry with combined assets of $1,000,000 or more

items.label: Placement Facility
items.detail: Coverage for employers unable to get it normally; every authorized comp insurer participates

items.label: Voluntary compensation endorsement
items.detail: Statutory-level benefits for workers the law doesn't require you to cover

beats.text: In Michigan, an employer insures with an authorized insurer or self-insures with the Workers' Disability Compensation Agency's authorization. 2 or more employers in one industry with combined assets of $1,000,000 or more may self-insure as a group.
beats.say: In Michigan, an employer insures with an authorized insurer or self-insures with the Workers' Disability Compensation Agency's authorization. Two or more employers in one industry with combined assets of one million dollars or more may self-insure as a group.

beats.text: The Placement Facility covers employers who can't get coverage normally; every authorized comp insurer must participate.
beats.say: The Placement Facility covers employers who can't get coverage normally; every authorized comp insurer must participate.

beats.text: Voluntary compensation pays comp-level benefits to workers you aren't required to cover, like farm or domestic workers.
beats.say: Voluntary compensation pays comp-level benefits to workers you aren't required to cover, like farm or domestic workers.

items: Comp is the exclusive remedy; only an intentional tort escapes it
Must carry: 3 at once, or 1 at 35 for 13 of 52 weeks; all public
Paid from day 8; from the injury date at 2 weeks; 80% after-tax AWW
Rails: FELA. Shore: Longshore Act. Ship's crew: Jones Act

beats.text: Let's recap: exclusive remedy, who must carry comp, day 8 and 80%, rails, shore and ship, and the premium formula.
beats.say: Let's recap: exclusive remedy, who must carry comp, day eight and eighty percent, rails, shore and ship, and the premium formula.
